expectations.text: Says the project must first decide whether it carries paid placements at all
expectations.evidence: "Decide that you take ads. Post one line in your maintainer channel ... Get 2+ maintainers to say yes in writing."

expectations.text: Names the per-issue cap and who approves sponsors as decisions to settle first
expectations.evidence: A cap of 2 secondary slots sits in the rate card. Neither the cap nor sponsor approval is flagged as a decision to settle first.

expectations.text: Points to the programme or charter decision as a separate step before selling
expectations.evidence: Step 1 is a written maintainer decision before the contract. "The contract below leans on that record."

expectations.text: Flags that without a fiscal host or invoicing entity the project cannot sell yet
expectations.evidence: It says "Use a fiscal host ... If you don't, the signer is a named individual. Make that a conscious choice." It does not block selling.

expectations.text: Declines prepaying six months of issues the irregular schedule may skip
expectations.evidence: It sells a 12-issue prepaid package at USD 4,000 and drafts the contract for it.

expectations.text: Recommends booking only issues the owner has committed to
expectations.evidence: It books all 12 issues. It only suggests "up to 12 Issues, pro-rata refund" as a possible change if nobody commits.

expectations.text: Requires a pause clause that moves or refunds slots
expectations.evidence: "If the schedule slips, your slots move with it" and §3.3 refund or extension for undelivered issues.

expectations.text: Writes or requires an acceptance policy before judging this sponsor
expectations.evidence: Only a placeholder list "We don't accept ads for [e.g. gambling...]". No written acceptance policy is required.

expectations.text: Asks about community norms or maintainer buy-in for commercial content
expectations.evidence: "Get 2+ maintainers to say yes in writing" and "Disclose it to the other maintainers first."

expectations.text: Requires a named seller with hours to answer, approve copy and report, given the volunteer-when-time-allows schedule
expectations.evidence: Only "Who will actually run the 12 issues?" No named seller with hours for answering, approving copy and reporting.

expectations.text: Notes a sellability check is needed (click data, reader description, seller hours)
expectations.evidence: "Subscriber count and open rate. The rate card needs them, and you must not invent them." Seller hours are not covered.

expectations.text: Does not deliver a final price as if the gate already passed
expectations.evidence: It delivers a complete rate card and a contract at "USD 4,000" for 12 issues.

expectations.text: Mentions taking payment before the copy deadline rather than long invoice terms for a small volunteer publisher, or prepay tied only to committed issues
expectations.evidence: Payment is invoiced on signing and due within 14 days, covering all 12 issues. It is not tied to committed issues or to the copy deadline.
